methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $105M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
EarthGrid is a Seed-stage Transportation company that has raised $105.3M to date. The relevant comp universe comprises six private frontier-transport firms including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Navier, and Olympian Motors; no public comparables exist in this niche.

Peer-Median valuation proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow peer overlap—while three same-sector peers exist, none satisfied stage or valuation-tier filters necessary for reliable median benchmarking. Consequently, Stage-Progression provided the sole applicable triangulation method. Using total raised ($105M) as a proxy for current value and applying a typical Seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.5x yields an implied valuation of $263M.

This analysis supports a valuation range of $224M to $303M, centered on $263M. The wide band reflects reliance on a single method and absence of transaction or peer-revenue data to corroborate the stage-progression assumption. Key uncertainties include whether the 2.5x multiplier accurately reflects EarthGrid's capital efficiency relative to Transportation frontier peers, and the absence of revenue or unit-economics data limits confidence in any floor valuation. Sensitivity to the multiplier assumption (±20%) drives the low and high bounds.
